comparator.name: Pedagogical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 adopted programme appendix governs the 60-EC compulsory first year and the shared second/third-year units. The generic bachelor offers Pedagogy/Educational Sciences and Orthopedagogy; the former is chosen as the broad upbringing-and-education route, not for UCR fit. A coherent 180 EC consists of 60 first-year EC, 50 individually listed common upper-year EC, 25 route EC, two explicitly permitted 2.5-EC research workshops, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC genuine minor choice. The appendix labels the common part 55 EC and the differentiated part 25 EC, although its individually listed common units total 50 EC and the route units plus workshops total 30 EC. The individually specified units and the 90-EC major total reconcile when the workshops are included; this grouping discrepancy is recorded rather than inventing an unnamed five-credit course. The general prospectus still displays older first-year course titles, so the current appendix governs the 2026–27 component identities.

core: Child and adolescent development, learning, cognition and behavioural difficulties, with psychological and social foundations
Upbringing, family environments, education, learning and social inequality, including the Pedagogy/Educational Sciences route
Qualitative and quantitative social-science research, assessment, statistical modelling, workshops and bachelor thesis

questions: How can schools and families support young people facing developmental or behavioural challenges?
How can educational practice and institutions respond to inequality?

trace: Introduces psychological and neural explanations of behaviour that underlie study of child development.

Introduces the sociological analysis of institutions, social relations, race and gender as foundations for examining the environments in which children grow up; it does not itself teach educational sociology.
Introduces administrative law, rights and justice as general legal foundations for evaluating public responsibilities toward children and education. It does not teach Dutch education law.
Provides empirical design and statistics for evaluating developmental and educational claims.
Explains social influence, relationships and group behaviour relevant to young people in families and schools.
Provides neurobiological foundations for cognition, behaviour and developmental study.
Teaches interviews and qualitative analysis applicable to researching families, schools and social contexts.
Develops measurement, experimental design and statistical inference used in behavioural research.
Investigates memory, attention and social cognition, which are important parts of learning and development.

Studies how stories about children and young people, including storybooks and educational institutions, have represented gender. This historical case complements the study of children’s social environments; it is not a history of pedagogy.

Teaches the design and delivery of persuasive speaking that students subsequently put to use with local primary-school children in Rhetoric in Action. This sequence supports that specific child-facing project, not professional pedagogical counselling.
Introduces psychological disorders and their evidence base as a limited perspective on developmental difficulties.
Directly studies cognitive, social, emotional and physical development from childhood and adolescence across the lifespan.
Examines perceptual and motor processing as specific dimensions of learning and development.
Includes the design and delivery of speaking and debate exercises with local primary-school children; it is not a pedagogical internship.
Studies young people’s resilience and supportive school environments through an actual research project for youth leaders and educators.

Examines biopsychosocial determinants of health and clinical health interventions across the lifespan. It adds a bounded health-psychology perspective on wellbeing and support for young people, without supplying child-specific pedagogy or treatment training.
Studies human-rights law and ethical claims relevant to the rights framework of children and education; it is not specialist education law.
Analyses motivation, group dynamics and organisational culture relevant to learning professionals and educational institutions.
Covers psychological assessment of infants, children and adolescents and interventions, without claiming orthopedagogical qualification.
Teaches systematic review and meta-analysis for evaluating intervention and educational research evidence.
Investigates language acquisition, bilingualism, reading and dyslexia as concrete aspects of children’s learning.
Develops ethical reasoning about duties, harm and responsibility in decisions affecting young people.

alternatives.label: Child development, social contexts and research
alternatives.concept: An academic UCR response combines developmental and social psychology, cognition, the sociology and gendered histories of children’s environments, a school-linked communication project, and qualitative and quantitative research. It offers related ways to study upbringing and education while lacking Groningen’s dedicated pedagogy sequence, educational-science methods and professional internship.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by psychology, cognition and social research, with a gender-history course and one school-linked practice course. The title describes those strengths without implying a sustained curriculum in educational sciences or professional pedagogy.
progression: The brain-and-behaviour foundation precedes its formally dependent psychology and cognition courses, and research/statistics precede organisational psychology. Introductory rhetoric precedes its child-facing applied project. Every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026–Spring 2029 term; 24 unique courses include eight 300-level courses and first-year PPD.

candidates.label: Orthopedagogical assessment and child support
candidates.reason: UCR has child-development psychology and general psychodiagnostics, already used where relevant in the closest response, but lacks the route’s sustained child-specific diagnostics, treatment, disability and family-therapy curriculum. A distinct 24-course orthopedagogical programme would rely on adjacent adult/general health courses as substitutes.

candidates.label: Academic primary-school teacher education
candidates.reason: The official route is an integrated four-year double degree with a teacher-education provider and practical qualification. UCR’s primary-school rhetoric project cannot supply that professional teaching sequence or credential; it cannot organise a defensible separate 24-course UCR programme.

routeSelection.basis: The generic 180-EC Pedagogical Sciences target does not name a route. The 2026–27 appendix offers Pedagogy/Educational Sciences and Orthopedagogy; the former broadly retains upbringing, education, family, social development and educational policy, whereas the latter is more specialised in diagnostics and intervention. The four-year primary-school teacher double degree is not the ordinary bachelor route. This choice precedes UCR course selection.

selection.assessment: The closest UCR programme uses the available developmental, cognitive, sociological and research curriculum without claiming specialist pedagogy. The orthopedagogy candidate cannot support a second child-specific clinical and intervention sequence, and the teacher-education candidate requires professional classroom training and a second degree that UCR does not offer. A further alternative is therefore not constructed.

notes.text: Groningen requires a dedicated sequence in pedagogy and educational sciences, programme-specific research workshops, a bachelor internship and a thesis. UCR can combine developmental psychology, cognition, sociology, communication and research, but does not reproduce the specialist pedagogical curriculum or professional practice route.
